platforms.name: italki
platforms.notes: Flat 15% on regular lessons. Trial lessons: 0% (tutor keeps 100%).

platforms.name: Preply
platforms.notes: Sliding scale: 33% at 0 hours → 18% after 400 hours teaching on Preply. First trial lesson: 100% to Preply (not modeled).

platforms.name: Cambly
platforms.notes: Per-minute pay: $0.17/min (~$10.20/hour). Effective hourly often lower ($5-8) due to gaps between calls.

platforms.name: ChampionTutor
platforms.notes: First-month commission. Agency-style introduction model — half of the first month's fee, then 0% thereafter.

platforms.name: MindFlex
platforms.notes: First-half-of-first-month commission. Agency model similar to ChampionTutor.

platforms.name: FamilyTutor
platforms.notes: Half of first month. Agency model.

platforms.name: Tueetor
platforms.notes: Lead-based — tutors purchase credits to view student requests. No commission per lesson.

platforms.name: Snapask
platforms.notes: Per-session flat rate: HK$5 per question answered (bonus tiers add HK$1/session per 25 questions above 200/month). Not a commission on tutor-set rates.

tax.self_employment_form: Form B (for self-employed sole proprietors), filed via myTax Portal
registration_steps: Register your business name (sole proprietorship) with ACRA via BizFile+ (https://www.bizfile.gov.sg) — annual fee S$60. Optional but recommended if trading under any name other than your own.

File income tax annually via myTax Portal (https://mytax.iras.gov.sg) using Form B — deadline 18 April for paper or 18 April online. Self-employed file under 'Trade, Business, Profession or Vocation'.
GST registration is required only if revenue exceeds S$1M/year. Voluntary registration is possible but adds compliance burden — most tutors should not register voluntarily.

CPF — Singapore Citizens and PRs must contribute to MediSave (the medical savings portion of CPF) on net trade income above S$6,000/year. Rate ~8-10.5% depending on age, capped at S$5,760-S$7,560/year.
Keep records of income and expenses for 5 years (IRAS requirement).
tax.notes: Singapore's tax regime is among the simplest globally for tutors: GST threshold is S$1M (most tutors never hit it), brackets are progressive but income tax effective rates are low under S$80K. Tax year is the calendar year. CPF MediSave contribution is the main 'extra' for citizens and PRs.

background_check.name: Tuition centre clearance via Singapore Police Force (Certificate of Clearance) — only required if registering with MOE-registered tuition centres
background_check.notes: Not legally required for private home tutoring. Parents and agencies sometimes request it. Apply via the SPF e-services portal; result valid 6 months. Fee S$80 (electronic copy).

payment_methods.name: PayNow
payment_methods.notes: Free, instant, peer-to-peer via mobile / NRIC / UEN. Default for domestic tutoring transactions. Available across all major SG banks.

payment_methods.name: FAST (bank transfer)
payment_methods.notes: Fast And Secure Transfers — free instant interbank transfers.

insurance.notes: Public liability is not legally required for home or online tuition but is recommended for tutors of minors or those operating from a fixed address. ~S$200-500/year for S$500K-1M cover. Professional indemnity (covering bad-advice claims) is optional and rarely purchased by individual tutors.
